candidates.title: Privacy commissioner to investigate Canadian Crime Stoppers breach
candidates.description: Privacy Commissioner Philippe Dufresne is opening an investigation into a massive Crime Stoppers data breach, his office said in a Tuesday statement. The probe is focused on Navigate 360, the U.S. third party that Crime Stoppers chapters worldwide had hired to manage and secure its anonymous tips.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: How will a new Conservative premier change the relationship between B.C. and Alberta?
candidates.description: The Conservatives taking power in British Columbia could help strengthen ties between the province and Alberta, but it could also spark competition between the provincial neighbours, some analysts say.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Big wins, shocking losses, and goodbye to a 46-year mayor: what to know about Ontario's 400+ elections
candidates.description: From a big night for women to a bad night for some Canada's longest-serving mayors, here are the key headlines and takeaways from the more than 400 municipal elections in Ontario on Monday.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Serial Calgary rapist from 1980s convicted of 9 offences against mothers, teen girl
candidates.description: A serial rapist who targeted vulnerable victims who were home alone with young children at the time they were attacked has been convicted of his crimes more than 40 years after the fact.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: P.E.I. man pleads not guilty to terrorism charges that police say are a 1st for Atlantic Canada
candidates.description: A man from Prince Edward Island has pleaded not guilty to what police have called the first terrorism charges ever laid in Atlantic Canada.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Ottawa Rapid FC pull merch naming nonexistent 'Van Blurené Parc'
candidates.description: Ever heard of Ottawa's Van Blurené Parc or gazed upon the giant sign on the national gallery? That alternate version of Ottawa was briefly on merchandise for the Ottawa Rapid soccer team before it was pulled.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Warrant out for long-term offender from Sask. who walked away from halfway house in B.C.
candidates.description: Mitchell Moise is wanted on a Canada-wide warrant after walking away from a halfway house in B.C. He is a long-term offender serving a sentence for violent offences committed almost 20 years ago in Saskatchewan.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Canadian forward Ben Kindel returns to Penguins practice after medical episode
candidates.description: Pittsburgh Penguins forward Ben Kindel returned to practice on Tuesday, a week after the 19-year-old fainted on the team's flight back from Utah.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: PQ accuses Ottawa of muzzling Quebec during upcoming Canada-EU summit
candidates.description: Quebec Premier Paul St-Pierre Plamondon is denouncing the federal government's refusal to allow him to speak at the Canada-EU summit which will begin in Montreal on Oct. 29.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Ottawa tables new MAID legislation, excluding people suffering solely from mental illness
candidates.description: Legislation tabled on Tuesday also sets criteria for people to make what's known as an "advance request" for medically assisted death, before losing the capacity to consent due to their health condition.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Q&A: Elections Alberta explains why the referendum took so long to count
candidates.description: Elections Alberta said more than 20 million ballots were counted in the days following the vote. That's more than any electoral event in Canadian history, including federal elections.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Ford says he feels 'badly' for Ont. students caught up in his government's financial aid program pause
candidates.description: On the first day back after a 147-day break from the Ontario legislature, provincial opposition parties spent much of question period calling for colleges and universities minister Nolan Quinn to be fired for his handling of the OSAP program.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Raptors say Kawhi Leonard will miss at least a week with swelling in his left knee
candidates.description: Kawhi Leonard will be sidelined for at least a week because of swelling in his left knee, the Toronto Raptors said Tuesday.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: B.C. teen starts free literacy program to combat AI reliance among peers
candidates.description: A Grade 12 student in Surrey, B.C., says she has helped hundreds of school-aged kids improve their literacy skills after starting a free program this year aimed at reducing AI reliance and encouraging critical thinking.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Yukon photographer captures footage of caribou carrying dead rival in its antlers
candidates.description: WARNING: This story contains graphic images of wildlife. Wildlife photographer Peter Mather said he was “shocked” to find a pair of bull caribou with antlers locked together, one of them dead, in the mountains south of Whitehorse earlier this month. He captured what happened as other wildlife fed off the carcass, still attached to the other bull.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Order of Hockey in Canada returns after multi-year hiatus, Hockey Canada announces
candidates.description: Hockey Canada is bringing back the Order of Hockey in Canada after a multi-year hiatus. A new nine-member selection committee, chaired by hockey broadcaster and producer John Shannon, will select three honourees each year based on their contributions to the growth and development of hockey in Canada.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Olivia Chow romps to victory as head of progressive new Toronto council
candidates.description: Olivia Chow will continue in the mayor's chair for another four years, after beating Brad Bradford. Chow won some 530,000 votes in an election where several of her key progressive allies also triumphed.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Molly Carlson made history by diving off an iceberg. Why she did it
candidates.description: Canadian cliff diver Molly Carlson becomes the first woman to dive off an iceberg. She recently scaled an iceberg off Newfoundland and dove into the Atlantic Ocean. Her sponsor, Red Bull, shared the dive for the first time last week.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Lawyers describe nuanced factors of addictions, mental health in Sask. manslaughter case
candidates.description: Keenan Starr was not taking his antipsychotic medication when he stabbed two relatives on Little Pine First Nation in a drunken rage, killing one of them.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: These midterm races will decide who controls U.S. Congress for the rest of Trump's presidency
candidates.description: The most important elections in next Tuesday's U.S. midterms will play out in just a handful of states and districts where polling suggests the Republicans and Democrats are in tight races.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Why a spate of gun-for-hire shootings in Toronto were likely paid for by Iran
candidates.description: A CBC News investigation has pinpointed a dozen politically-motivated gun-for-hire shootings in Toronto that appear to have been financed by the Iranian government.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: El Salvador has deployed roughly 1,000 soldiers to Haiti: security official
candidates.description: Around 1,000 soldiers from El Salvador have been sent to Haiti in a string of deployments in recent days after four Salvadoran members of the UN-backed force in Haiti went missing, a security official ‌in Haiti told Reuters on Tuesday.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Meet Canada's 5 Eurovision finalists
candidates.description: Five finalists — William Cloutier, Josiane, Rêve, Talk and Tyler Shaw — are competing to become Canada’s first Eurovision entrant in 2027. Canadians can watch their performances online and vote up to 10 times before voting closes Nov. 5.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Trump rallies are still rockin' with Neil Young's music — so he's suing, again
candidates.description: Neil Young is once again suing over Rockin' in the Free World being played at U.S. President Donald Trump's political rallies, six years after their last go-around about the blistering anthem.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Brazil's Flávio Bolsonaro headed to the U.S. after losing election, sources say
candidates.description: Brazilian Senator Flávio Bolsonaro has left the country for the United States after losing Sunday's presidential election and refusing ‌to comply with a Supreme Court order to hand over his passports, two sources said.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Canadian 'tremendously sorry' after spending stolen crypto on Lamborghini, BMWs, jewelry
candidates.description: A 20-year-old Canadian who conned cryptocurrency holders out of millions of dollars — and lived large as a teenager in Florida with "extravagant" partying, access to a private jet and luxury cars — could soon be headed home to Canada after he pleaded guilty to a money laundering conspiracy and was sentenced to time served Monday.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: IN PHOTOS | Rise and fall of Hunter's Moon
candidates.description: October's full moon has been a delight for stargazers. Check out some of the best images of this celestial event around the world.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Canada, U.A.E. sign defence, energy agreements during crown prince's visit
candidates.description: Canada and the United Arab Emirates signed a handful of trade and infrastructure agreements during the crown prince of Abu Dhabi's visit to Ottawa.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Israelis shatter turnout records in election that will pass wartime judgment on Netanyahu
candidates.description: Israelis surged to the polls on Tuesday at a pace that shattered records, to pass wartime judgment on Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu in what voters described as the most consequential election in the nation's history.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Ebola cases top 10,000 in Democratic Republic of Congo, as countries race to stop spread
candidates.description: The fast-moving Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo has reached 10,000 confirmed cases, government data showed Tuesday, as health authorities race to slow the spread of the disease in multiple African countries.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Russia, Ukraine begin ceasefire in city of Oleshky as deadly strikes continue elsewhere
candidates.description: Russia and Ukraine began a regional ceasefire to allow the start of a humanitarian effort in the Russian-occupied town of ‌Oleshky, both sides said Tuesday, but both sides engaged in strikes elsewhere, including the Ukrainian capital of Kyiv.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: U.K. charges 2 men, accuses them of working on Iran's behalf in incident at airbase
candidates.description: Two men were charged Tuesday with national security offences over a suspected plot against RAF Fairford, a U.S.-run military airbase in England, police and prosecutors said.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Chinese brands cut ties with French soccer star Mbappe over 'Chinese dictator' remark
candidates.description: French soccer star Kylian Mbappe's face appears in ads across China, from subway stations to inside elevators, but now at least three companies are cutting ties with the national team captain after he made some comments apparently referring to Mao Zedong, the founding leader of Communist China, as a dictator.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Lula re-elected in Brazil as Bolsonaro rejects results
candidates.description: Brazil's President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, a vocal critic of U.S. President Donald Trump, was re-elected Sunday in a result that provides relief to critics of widening U.S. influence in Latin America.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: UN commission says Israel has continued to commit genocide in Gaza since truce
candidates.description: A United Nations commission says Israel ​continued to commit genocide in Gaza after last October's U.S.-brokered ceasefire in the enclave, in a report published Monday that Israel dismissed as part of a "misinformation campaign."
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: U.S. officials accuse Canada of midterm meddling — but Trump has endorsed foreign candidates
candidates.description: Despite U.S. officials repeatedly warning Canada not to get involved in the upcoming U.S. midterms, U.S. President Donald Trump has his own track record of weighing in on foreign elections.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: How this Brooklyn bar owner had Conan O'Brien in stitches on SubwayTakes
candidates.description: Debbie Shields took a seat on a New York City subway and ended up joking with comedian Conan O'Brien about their fictional family. Their exchange on internet talk show SubwayTakes went viral. The Brooklyn bar owner says she's always making people laugh, but this experience was surreal.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Anthropic files for potentially biggest IPO ever, even as CEO warns of AI risks to humanity
candidates.description: Artificial intelligence giant Anthropic filed papers on Monday for what could be the biggest initial public offering of stock ever.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Nigeria Ebola patient flown to Switzerland, Congo health worker killed as 4 countries deal with outbreak
candidates.description: Officials on opposite sides of the African continent are trying to determine how a woman diagnosed with Ebola in Nigeria's capital last week contracted the deadly virus without having visited the Democratic Republic of Congo — the epicentre of one of the worst human outbreaks of the virus in history.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Cleveland-Cliffs says Stelco in 'full compliance' with commitments to Ottawa, wants to meet with Joly

candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Microsoft gives voluntary buyout offer to about 60,000 employees

candidates.title: Norway and Finland leaders hold rare call with Putin
candidates.description: An end to the conflict in Ukraine "will not be achieved through silence," Finland's President Alexander Stubb said.

candidates.title: Mbappé sorry for 'ill-judged' Mao remark after backlash in China

candidates.title: Dutch zookeeper dies after being mauled in leopard enclosure

candidates.title: How Kane defied doubters to become world's best

candidates.title: Israel and the US are both going to the polls - the consequences will be global

candidates.description: Several thousand properties in the north of Scotland are still without power after days of high winds and heavy rain.

candidates.description: About 40% of the plants and animals in protected sites across Northern Ireland fall short of meeting the standard for "favourable condition".

candidates.title: Scotland's recycling rates at five-year low. How is your area doing?

candidates.title: Part of Antarctica named after former BBC science correspondent

candidates.title: What to know about China's plenum as Xi seeks stronger party discipline
candidates.description: This closed-door gathering that started Monday comes about a year before Xi is expected to secure a fourth term and personnel changes to key leadership bodies.

candidates.title: Retriever-Free Retrieval: Navigating Documents with Decision Models
candidates.description: While language models have become dramatically more capable, retrieval still largely relies on lexical matching or similarity in fixed embedding spaces. This creates a capability asymmetry: what the retriever fails to find, even the strongest generator cannot recover. We propose DecisionRAG, which brings the capabilities of pretrained language models to retrieval using decision models that jointly evaluate candidate branches in a single forward pass, without generating any tokens, and show that judging candidates in a shared context makes their relevance estimates comparable. Like a person browsing a library, DecisionRAG navigates the corpus's inherent structure from broad topics down to individual passages, deciding at each level which branches are worth exploring. Without task-specific training or a first-stage retriever, DecisionRAG outperforms dense retrieval with an 8B reranker by 13.8 R@1 points on MultiDoc2Dial and 17.4 Hit@1 points on Natural Questions. Across four benchmarks, including a corpus of 2.68 million Wikipedia paragraphs, retrieval takes just 0.7-1.8 seconds per query.
candidates.author: Chao Wan, Paul Jünger, Beixi Du, Bodong Liu, Navaneetha Krishnan, Kilian Q. Weinberger

candidates.title: Center-of-Mass Interpretation of Evolution Strategies
candidates.description: Evolution strategies (ES) update a model by sampling a population of perturbed copies, scoring each one, and moving in the reward-weighted direction of the perturbations. This update is usually presented as an estimate of a smoothed gradient. We present a geometrical interpretation of this update instead. Treat each perturbed model as a particle and its reward as the particle's mass. Before scoring, every particle has the same mass and the population balances at its centroid. Once rewards are assigned, it balances at its reward-weighted center of mass instead. We show that the mean-subtracted ES update is exactly this displacement, scaled by a scalar factor that depends on the mean reward, for any finite population. The physical reading needs nonnegative rewards, which can always be arranged by adding a constant to every reward without changing the update. In the limit of a large population or under antithetic sampling, the centroid sits on the model itself, so ES has an even simpler geometric interpretation: from its current location, the model moves towards the reward-weighted center of mass of its own population. The same picture explains what subtracting the mean reward does: it changes the point from which the displacement is measured, from the model to the sampled centroid. Our contribution is an intuitive, geometric way to visualize an ES update, exact for any finite population.
candidates.author: Akshat Gupta

candidates.title: Learning Force-Reactive Humanoid Loco-Manipulation
candidates.description: Many everyday tasks require controlling contact force as well as motion. On a humanoid, this force must often be coordinated across both hands and the whole body, and cannot be specified by kinematic trajectories alone. Therefore, we present FLORE, a framework for learning force-reactive humanoid loco-manipulation. We collect robot-free demonstrations using two force-sensing UMI-style handheld grippers for hand motion and contact wrenches, and wearable trackers for body motion. A force-reactive diffusion policy takes vision, proprioception, and measured wrenches as input, then predicts actions and per-hand force commands. A hybrid compliance whole-body controller with force tracking executes these commands while maintaining balance: an integral of the force error measured by real force/torque (F/T) sensors lets each hand track force accurately along the commanded direction and remain compliant along the others. In simulation, the controller tracks per-hand force commands of varied magnitude and direction, with little loss in whole-body motion accuracy. Across three contact-rich tasks on the robot, the force-reactive policy succeeds in 80% of rollouts, compared with 26.7% for a position-only policy trained on the same demonstrations and executed by the same controller. For more details, please visit our website: https://louis-leee.github.io/FLoRe/.
candidates.author: Sihang Li, Xiaofeng Guo, Jinkun Cao, Charlie Cheng, Ruihan Yang, Chen Feng, Guanya Shi, Haozhi Qi

candidates.title: Differentiable Contact Dynamics for Legged Locomotion: Policy Learning and Contact-Implicit Trajectory Optimization
candidates.description: This paper proposes a smooth analytic gradient for frictional contact and applies it to policy learning and contact-implicit trajectory optimization for legged locomotion. The exact contact sensitivity is available in closed form but describes changes within the current contact mode, providing no first-order information toward neighboring contact modes. The proposed gradient replaces this sensitivity only in the backward pass, leaving the hard-contact forward solve unchanged and the realized rollout feasible. A central-path relaxation of the de Saxcé-corrected second-order-cone complementarity problem for Coulomb friction smooths the conditions defining the separating, clamping, and sliding modes. The relaxed sensitivity is evaluated at a point on the central path obtained by a Newton iteration initialized from the hard-contact solution. The sensitivity remains continuous through contact-mode transitions and converges to the exact sensitivity as the relaxation vanishes. Using 100,000 samples and less than 2 min of training on a desktop PC, policy learning with the proposed gradient produces a policy that transfers to hardware without fine-tuning. On hardware, the robot under a trotting policy withstands pushes and traverses debris and slippery ground. In trajectory optimization, the proposed gradient reaches contact-rich solutions missed by exact and Signorini-relaxed gradients. Project page: https://diffcontact.github.io
candidates.author: Gijeong Kim, Seungbin Oh, Dongyun Kang, Hae-Won Park

candidates.title: Nonprehensile Robotic Catching Using Virtual Constraints
candidates.description: The problem of nonprehensile robotic catching is addressed using virtual nonholonomic constraints (VNHCs); the motion of the robot end-effector is designed and controlled directly in terms of the states of the object before it is caught on the surface of the end-effector. In contrast to contemporary approaches, our approach avoids the need for object trajectory prediction, and consequent time-varying robot trajectory generation. With a focus on the planar case, we demonstrate that our VNHC approach can be used to catch an object on an end-effector at a desired height, with minimal relative normal velocity at the contact instant. Moreover, the VNHC function depends only on the desired catching height, and the same VNHC can be used for a range of initial conditions. We use model predictive control (MPC) to bring the object and end-effector to rest at a desired location after contact is made. The approach is validated in simulation.
candidates.author: Aakash Khandelwal, Ranjan Mukherjee

candidates.title: OSWAM: An Effective World Action Model with One-Step Action Generation
candidates.description: Direct-policy World Action Models (WAM) have demonstrated the benefits of decoupling action generation from explicit future visual prediction for efficient inference in autonomous driving and embodied control. However, they still require tens of denoising steps to achieve competitive action quality, incurring substantial latency and hindering real-time deployment. Simply reducing the number of denoising steps will collapse the nonlinear multi-step denoising trajectory into coarse updates, substantially degrading action quality. To reduce the denoising steps while enabling real-time action generation, we present an effective world action model with one-step action generation, namely OSWAM, for autonomous driving and embodied control. We argue that it is the absence of structured action priors in random noise initialization that forces direct-policy WAMs to recover coherent action sequences through iterative denoising. Hence, we construct imagination tokens to initialize the diffusion process, providing physical priors and action-conditioned representations. We further introduce privileged information distillation with future conditioning to enhance future-aware action generation. As a result, OSWAM can efficiently and effectively generate high quality actions in just one diffusion step. Our experiments demonstrate that OSWAM achieves comparable or even better results in both autonomous driving and embodied control than direct-policy WAM and Joint-WAM that require tens of steps. It obtains approximately $3\times$ speedup over direct-policy WAM baselines and supports real-time compiled inference with latency as low as 40ms on an NVIDIA RTX 5090 GPU. The project page is available at https://gwenzhang.github.io/OSWAM/
candidates.author: Guowen Zhang, Liyi Chen, Xu Hu, Pengfei Wang, Jingfan Chen, Chenhang He, Lei Zhang

candidates.title: Patient-specific rubric-based evaluation of large language models across longitudinal cancer care
candidates.description: Large language models (LLMs) show promise in specialty medicine, yet existing evaluations largely focus on isolated clinical encounters rather than tracking how clinical responsibilities evolve across a longitudinal care pathway. Here we introduce NPC-RubricBench, a phase-aware benchmark for evaluating multistage clinical reasoning across the cancer care continuum, using nasopharyngeal carcinoma as a defined disease context. Curated from longitudinal records of 405 patients across two cancer centers, the benchmark comprises 941 patient-phase units across six sequential care phases and 17,688 patient-specific atomic criteria spanning five evaluation dimensions, with each assessment strictly restricted to decision-time clinical evidence. Evaluating 30 general-purpose and medical LLMs revealed that strong diagnostic performance does not carry over to downstream care. We evaluated 30 general-purpose and medical LLMs, showing that high diagnostic performance did not translate into improved downstream care. Instead, the dominant failure modes reversed across phases. Explicit decision errors dominated anatomical staging at 48.2%, whereas decision omissions dominated initial work-up and post-treatment follow-up at 33.4% and 30.4%, respectively. In the evaluated model set, medically adapted models showed higher omission rates than general-purpose models. Moreover, varying query granularity exposes a critical specification trade-off: broad open-ended requests degrade Decision Quality across all 30 models, while more detailed, checklist-like prompts raise Decision Quality but reduce Evidence Faithfulness and Safety Adherence. Furthermore, NPC-RubricBench demonstrates that static diagnostic benchmarks are insufficient to ensure consistent clinical reliability over time, highlighting the importance of phase-adaptive safeguards in multistage medical AI.
candidates.author: Wei-Wei Zhang, Pengkai Wang, Yan Li, Zhijie Sang, Guan-Qun Zhou, Jun-Yan Li, Shu-Han Zhou, Pei-Wen Liu, Ting-Xi Tang, Min Tang, Zhitian Hou, Jianmin Wu, Jian Guan, i Lin, Hongxia Yang, Ying Sun

candidates.title: Preserve to Expand: Source-Aware Adaptation and Model Merging for Multilingual LLM-Based ASR
candidates.description: Expanding multilingual ASR systems to new languages is challenging when adaptation must preserve previously supported languages without replaying source-language training data. We study this problem in connector-based Speech LLMs, where a trainable connector maps speech representations into a frozen large language model. We evaluate target-update construction and merging strategies for adapting the connector while preserving source-language performance. In single-target expansion, target-only fine-tuning and standard TIES merging learn new languages but cause severe source-language forgetting, while SSU-Wanda+TIES gives the best source-preserving trade-off. In multi-target expansion, update merging provides stable source retention, whereas recursive expansion can improve target adaptation under favorable orders but is highly order-sensitive. These results show that multilingual ASR expansion requires balancing target acquisition, source retention, and interactions among target-language updates.
candidates.author: Yuchen Zhang, Haralambos Mouratidis, Ravi Shekhar

candidates.title: I-HITL: Inalienable Human-in-the-Loop
candidates.description: Human oversight is a pillar of AI safety. It is often exercised by a human in the loop (HITL) who approves critical actions taken by an AI agent. AI agents' increasing ability to bypass guardrails, though, raises the question of how to enforce HITL robustly. We introduce the concept of inalienable human-in-the-loop (I-HITL). An I-HITL protocol ensures that an agent can initiate an action only with explicit human approval, even when the human interacts with a system (e.g., a local agentic harness) compromised by the agent. A strong I-HITL protocol additionally ensures such approval even when an adversarial human attempts to delegate approvals to an agent. To motivate I-HITL, we report on experiments with a popular agentic wallet platform in which raising an agent's spending cap requires HITL approval via emailed one-time passcodes (OTPs). Given access to the user's email and a task blocked by the cap, we find that ten different frontier models will often autonomously raise the cap, harvesting OTPs to bypass a HITL guardrail and surfacing other vulnerabilities. We formally define I-HITL using the concept of communication topologies and prove necessary and sufficient conditions for its realization. We show that an I-HITL protocol requires a trusted entity - a trusted computing device (or equivalent) - and characterize which such devices can and cannot realize an I-HITL protocol. We present a prototype I-HITL system called Countersign that can plug into and strengthen existing HITL systems using off-the-shelf consumer mobile devices.
candidates.author: Samuel Breckenridge, Dani Vilardell, Wenhao Wang, Fan Zhang, Ari Juels

candidates.title: Profiling a Frontier Agent with EBench: From Direct Control to Harness with Policy
candidates.description: Frontier multimodal large language models (MLLMs) can control robots without robot-specific training, but how their capabilities compare and interact with post-trained vision-language-action (VLA) and world action model (WAM) policies across manipulation demands remains to be thoroughly evaluated. In this report, we evaluate GPT-6-Astra on EBench as the core of an agent that controls a robot through an agent harness under the same visual and proprioceptive observation protocol as post-trained policies. We study two agent configurations: direct control, in which the agent generates waypoint commands directly, and harness with policy, in which it can also invoke a post-trained VLA or WAM policy for action execution. Under direct control, the agent achieves competitive overall performance relative to post-trained policies. It leads on short-horizon tasks and exhibits the least performance variation across generalization dimensions, whereas it underperforms post-trained policies on long-horizon tasks, tabletop manipulation, and high-precision contact-rich tasks. In the harness with policy, invoking a post-trained VLA or WAM combines the complementary strengths of both components, raising overall task success to the level of the strongest compared post-trained policies while substantially reducing token cost. However, performance remains below the per-task upper bound of the standalone components due to suboptimal policy invocation, fixed-instruction execution without subgoals, and grasp disruption when the agent resumes control. Overall, our study characterizes the capability boundary of a frontier MLLM agent and suggests directions for improving future agent harness design. Project page: https://internrobotics.github.io/EBench-Astra-Tech-Report/
candidates.author: Yifei Yao, Yude Zou, Guanbo Jiao, Xing Gao, Ning Gao, Yukai Wang, Jiantong Chen, Zihou Zhu, Xinyu Li, Ningyu Yan, Shuai Wang, Jianming Ma, Haoyu Guo, Weinan Zhang, Chunhua Shen

candidates.title: Reva: Real-Time Vulnerability Detection through Contextual Probing of Large Language Models
candidates.description: A vulnerability costs more to fix the later it is discovered. As coding agents generate code faster than developers can review it, software needs a first line of defense screening each new function in real time. LLM agents have recently become capable of finding real-world vulnerabilities by working as a security expert would: they run analysis tools, explore the surrounding code, test hypotheses and weigh the evidence before forming their own judgement. This reasoning, however, spans many model calls, so that each verdict takes minutes of compute, far too long for real-time screening. Faster detectors, which fine-tune deep learning models or prompt an LLM for a direct verdict, are less accurate: they judge a function without the context an agent gathers, and an LLM's generated verdict is unreliable even when given some of it. We present REVA (REal-time Vulnerability Analysis), an AI vulnerability detector that brings the security context and code understanding components behind agentic detectors into a single forward pass of an LLM. For each new function, REVA gives the LLM a pre-computed threat model of its module, lightweight static analysis findings and call-graph information. REVA leverages a trained probe to read the LLM's internal representations of the new function in this context. On PrimeVul's held-out test set, REVA on GLM-5.3-Flash reaches 60.0% accuracy in about one second per function. This matches VulTriage (59.2%), the state-of-the-art agentic detector, run on the same LLM, while being over 250 times faster and less than a tenth as costly. On the same prompt, the probe is 14% to 17% more accurate than the LLM's own direct verdict. Across three open LLMs, REVA is at least as accurate as VulTriage, and about 10% more accurate on two of them. An LLM's internal representations thus encode much of what agentic detectors obtain through reasoning.
candidates.author: Amine Lbath, Massih-Reza Amini

candidates.title: Understanding Jev-Style System One Models: Does Structure Reduce Selection Bias?
candidates.description: Selection bias in large language models (LLMs) can persist despite instructions to ignore presentation order or prompts that elicit reasoning. Recent efforts to reproduce Jev-style System One behavior have produced a growing family of models that predict probabilities directly over supplied candidates. Yet systematic comparisons of selection bias across Jev versions, Jev reproductions, and generative LLMs remain limited in multi-option tasks. This leaves a central question: does Jev-style decision structure reduce selection bias? We address this question with a simple test that shuffles options while keeping question and candidate content fixed. Across two Jev versions, twelve Jev reproductions, and six generative LLMs, we trace individual answers through eight presentations and compare them with fixed-order repetition. On our primary collection of 1,700 questions from two benchmarks, Jev's accuracy varies by less than two percentage points, yet its cumulative failure set expands by 27--29\% relative to the original order, with first failures continuing into the final presentation. This loss of initial successes is substantially larger than under fixed-order repetition, even for highly repeatable Jev reproductions. Nor does Jev show a general advantage over the LLM baselines in preserving correct choices. Aggregation offers limited protection: voting yields modest gains for Jev, while even unanimous answers are frequently wrong. These results expose a gap between repeatable decisions and decisions that remain correct across equivalent presentations, showing why stable accuracy alone cannot establish resistance to selection bias.
candidates.author: Mingyang Song, Mao Zheng, Zhiyuan Ma, Xinpeng Zhou
